policy.detail: IMDA Green Data Centre Roadmap (30 May 2024) targets PUE of 1.3 or lower. At least 300 MW of new capacity is allocated competitively, with applicants showing low-carbon energy plans.
PUE target of 1.25 for large facilities by 2025; East Data West Computing (2022) steers new build to western provinces with solar and wind.

Effective moratorium on new Dublin-area grid connections from 2021. For applications after 12 December 2025, new sites must meet at least 80% of annual demand with additional Irish renewables on a six-year glide path and hold dispatchable generation or storage.

Five AI Growth Zones (Culham, North East England, North Wales, South Wales, North Lanarkshire). The government rejected a call for a moratorium on 28 August 2026 while saying support is not a blank cheque. No universal water-use disclosure requirement exists; a report has called for one. Ofgem proposals on grid connection fees are still consultation-stage.

New York's legislature passed a one-year moratorium (4 June 2026) and Governor Hochul paused certain permits for sites of 50 MW or more (14 July 2026). Texas announced a pause on approvals pending a grid audit (10 August 2026). Maine's moratorium was vetoed. Port Washington (Wisconsin), Holyoke (Massachusetts), Seattle and others have local limits. No federal moratorium has advanced.
policy.note: Single tertiary source; verify each item before relying on it.

ethical_issues.detail: Concern that households bear grid upgrade costs. Federal bills such as the Ratepayer Protection Act would make data centres pay full costs.
Local supply strain; many jurisdictions lack mandatory water reporting.
On-site gas generation raises local air-quality concerns.
Complaints about secrecy in siting and tax deals; a proposed Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act would require public reporting on energy, water and emissions.

opposition.summary: Local opposition is now widespread. Wikipedia reports protests in 42 US states in July 2026 and about US$156 billion of projects delayed or cancelled in 2025 by local opposition, while a cited source title gives US$64 billion; treat the figures as unverified.
